title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from the margins and the computation. A is a curve of genus 1, i.e. an elliptic curve with origin 0, because Δ² = χ(A) = 0. P is an auxiliary variety and Y = A×P, so A×Y = A×A×P. There are two projections: t : A×Y → A and p : A×Y → Y, with p = p'×id_P where p' : A×A → A is the second projection. K denotes the degree of a 0-cycle.

The cycles. Θ = Θ_0×1_P, where Θ_0 = Δ − A×0 − 0×A on the surface A×A. This is the normalized diagonal: the Künneth H¹⊗H¹ part of the diagonal, essentially the class of the Poincaré divisor, written as a correspondence. c is a cycle on Y and c' = 1_A×c.

The page starts from an earlier formula, s_ℓ(g²) = t_*(Θ²·c'). Taking degrees and using the projection formula gives K(g²) = K(Θ²·(1_A×c)) = K(p_*(Θ²)·c).

Computing Θ_0². Expanding the square and using Δ² = 0 (self-intersection formula: deg of the normal bundle of Δ = 2g−2 = 0), (A×0)² = (0×A)² = 0, and Δ·(A×0) = Δ·(0×A) = (A×0)·(0×A) = (0,0) gives Θ_0² = −2(0,0). In general one gets Θ_0² = −2g·(point) on J×J-type situations.

Hence p_*(Θ²) = p'_*(Θ_0²)×1_P = −2(0×P) on A×P; Grothendieck writes −2(0×0×P), mixing A×A×P and A×P notation. Therefore K(s(g²)) = −2·c(0,0), where c(0,0) = K(c·(0×0×P)).

The counterexample. Choosing c = A×(a) with a ∈ P(k), written A×A×(a), gives c(0,0) = 1. Replacing c by −c then gives the values −2 and +2.

Purpose. The page refutes a would-be sign or positivity statement: that the degree K(s_ℓ(g²)) of some square, built from a correspondence/cycle g depending on c through Θ, has constant sign. This sits in the cluster of sign and positivity questions around Weil's positivity of the Rosati involution and the Hodge standard conjecture. The lesson, marked by "!!", is that a naive positivity for squares (without transposition or Lefschetz/primitive twisting, or for non-effective parameters) fails already for an elliptic curve. The quantity turns out to be linear in c, which makes the sign change trivial once computed.
errors: Notational slip: p_*(Θ²) should live on Y = A×P, i.e. −2(0×P), but it is written −2(0×0×P). Similarly c is said to be a cycle on Y but written c = A×A×(a); this is presumably c' = 1_A×c, or c = A×(a). The degree c(0,0) = 1 is correct under either reading.

The sign flip is obtained by replacing c by −c, i.e. a non-effective cycle. So the 'counterexample' only refutes a statement meant for arbitrary (not effective or positive) cycles c. Since the final expression is linear in c, this is automatic, and it suggests the expected positivity was being tested in a regime where it could not hold.
The identity Δ² = 0 is justified by χ(A) = 0 (the topological Euler characteristic of a genus-1 curve). This is correct; the reason given in the margin is partly illegible.

ideas.what: Computation of the self-intersection of the normalized diagonal Θ_0 = Δ − A×0 − 0×A on E×E: Θ_0² = −2·(point)
ideas.modern_name: Künneth (1,1)-component of the diagonal / Poincaré class; self-intersection −2g
ideas.where_published: Related material in Grothendieck, 'Sur une note de Mattuck–Tate' (1958) and 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969), but not this exact computation

ideas.what: Using the projection formula and the product decomposition p = p'×id_P to reduce the degree of s(g²) to a local intersection number c(0,0)
ideas.modern_name: projection formula for proper pushforward of cycles

ideas.what: Testing a putative sign/positivity property of a quadratic expression in correspondences, and finding it indefinite
ideas.modern_name: sign conditions for trace forms on correspondences; Hodge standard conjecture / Weil positivity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil (positivity of Rosati); Grothendieck & Bombieri (standard conjectures, 1968–69)
ideas.where_published: Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles (Bombay Colloquium 1968, publ. 1969)

deep.surprise_reason: A routine intersection computation on E×E×P, used to discard a naive sign statement. The failure is essentially forced by linearity in c, and nothing here goes beyond the known framework of the standard conjectures.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 's_\ell(g^2) = t_*(\Theta^2 c')' is consistent with the image; the following illegible words likely read 'la projection. Comme ... alors ..., d'où il résulte que ...' (uncertain).
In the margin the original first wrote 'A × Y → Y' with the Y struck through and overwritten.
'compte tenu que Δ² = 0 (égalité ... ) χ(A) = 0': the bracketed note seems to say Δ² equals the Euler characteristic ('égalité des ... / [nombre] ... χ(A) = 0').
'et la formule cherchée devient' is probably 'et la formule précédente devient'.
